story.head: Bring a pillow
paras: The Blues won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-4 in Detroit on Oct 31. The Red Wings (7-7-3) lost 2-1 to Vegas on Thursday, and the Blues (7-7-2) lost 5-4 in overtime to New Jersey the same night. Going in, the Wings are last in the Atlantic (20th in the NHL) and the Blues sixth in the Central (tied for 21st).
The Red Wings have played better than their record (.500) says: their chances are worth about .597, and their finishing has held them back. So have the Blues (.500 on chances worth .561).

The Red Wings block more shots than almost anyone (2nd), leave the shooting to their forwards (3rd lowest) and draw more penalties than they take (3rd). As for the Blues, they keep things calm after the whistle (lowest) and ice the puck less than almost anyone (3rd). They also have struggled on the power play (31st), so the Red Wings’ power play bites, but their doesn’t. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Alex DeBrincat (7 G / 9 A / 16 P in 17 GP) leads the Red Wings in scoring, and Viktor Arvidsson (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 17 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Blues, Mason McTavish (7 G / 5 A / 12 P in 16 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Jimmy Snuggerud (8 G / 3 A / 11 P in 16 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Daniil Tarasov (2-2-2 / .930 SV% in 5 GS) has been terrific for Detroit and will likely start. Joel Hofer (6-4-1 / .918 SV% in 11 GS) has been outstanding for St. Louis and will likely start.

items.text: The Red Wings are newly without John Gibson, and have been without Marco Kasper, Dylan Larkin, Jacob Bernard-Docker and Mason Appleton for several games. Daniil Tarasov is expected to start.
The Blues have been without Logan Mailloux for several games.
J.T. Compher has four goals in six games against St. Louis since 2023-24.
With Dylan Larkin out, Emmitt Finnie took 20 faceoffs in the Red Wings’ last game. He had been taking about three a game.
